result.title: Large Language Model Assisted Transportation Planning through a Differentiable User Equilibrium Layer
result.summary: Transportation planning has traditionally required substantial expertise in network modeling, traffic assignment, and optimization. As a result, strategic analyses such as network design, capacity expansion, and model calibration remain inaccessible to non-expert decision makers. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) provide an opportunity to bridge this gap by enabling natural-language interaction with complex transportation planning tools. However, existing LLM-based systems primarily serve as interfaces to simulation software and lack the ability to efficiently search, evaluate, and optimize transportation solutions. This study proposes an integrated human-AI transportation planning framework that combines a large language model, a model context protocol (MCP) interface, an open-source transportation planning engine (AequilibraE), and a differentiable user equilibrium (UE) assignment layer. The framework allows non-expert users to execute network analyses and improve solutions for optimization. A differentiable UE layer is developed by directly differentiating the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions of the Beckmann traffic assignment problem. The proposed framework is demonstrated through two representative planning tasks: calibration of travel time functions from observed traffic counts and network design under budget constraints. The examples illustrate how differentiable transportation models and LLM agents can jointly democratize transportation planning and substantially reduce barriers between domain expertise and transportation decision making.

AI.brief_summary: 该研究搭建了一个 LLM 智能体 + MCP 接口 + 开源交通规划引擎的可交互规划框架，并通过对 Beckmann 交通分配问题 KKT 条件直接求导构造可微用户均衡层，用出行时间函数标定与预算约束下的网络设计两个任务做示范。
AI.relevance_reason: 其可微均衡层本质上是对隐式不动点方程求导以获得梯度，可能为 latent 迭代推理状态的训练、梯度回传与贡献分配提供方法线索，但论文面向交通规划应用，与 LVR 状态生成的实际关联需人工核查。
